overview: The NebuLink Module NLN500b is the smallest STM32WL based LoRa module. It is built on the STM32WL SoC, which has an embedded LoRaWAN transceiver, for a wide range of smart applications where long range is required.
It operates in the 865/868 MHz band and uses the LoRa (Long-Range) and Sigfox protocols for communication, offering long range, low power and secure data transmission for M2M and IoT applications.

The module is designed to be extremely low-power and is based on the high-performance Arm® Cortex®-M4 32-bit RISC core operating at a frequency of up to 48 MHz. It is solder-ready on a 1.27 mm pitch SMD footprint with an RF shield, supports over-the-air firmware updates and offers u.FL, spring antenna and feedline antenna options.

LoRaWAN® and Sigfox™ on one hardware platform.
8 mA in RX mode; 146 mA TX at +21 dBm, 106 mA TX at +13 dBm.

features.d: Just 26.68 × 16.0 × 3.6 mm — a footprint comparable to a standard SIM card.
Supports both the LoRaWAN® and Sigfox™ protocols in the 865/868 MHz band.
−136 dBm sensitivity (DR0 / SF12) and more than 10 km line-of-sight range.
8 mA in RX mode; 146 mA TX at +21 dBm and 106 mA TX at +13 dBm; 1.8 V to 3.6 V supply.
9 × 12-bit ADC channels at 2.5 Msps and up to 21 digital I/O pins, 5 V tolerant.
Hardware encryption for secure data transmission in M2M and IoT applications.
Over-the-air firmware update capable, with serial-wire debug (SWD) and JTAG programming.
1.27 mm pitch SMD, directly soldered on any device board, with an RF shield on the module.

apps.d: Long-range, low-power connectivity for utility and consumption metering.
Field and crop monitoring where cellular coverage is limited.
Compact wireless connectivity for industrial monitoring and control.
Secure machine-to-machine data links for a wide range of IoT products.
